title: Major banks and miners lead ASX 200 to highest close since mid-June
text:

A key jobs figure released in the United States led to the ASX “ripping higher” during Friday’s trading, led by the major banks and miners.

On a strong day of trading the benchmark ASX 200 rallied 119.90 points or 1.37 per cent higher to 8844.40, its highest close since it fell from 9000 points in mid June.

The broader All Ordinaries also jumped 117.40 points or 1.31 per cent to 9048, while the Australian dollar added 0.47 per cent to buy 69.47 US cents.

Dominating the Australian sharemarket was news out of the US, which showed hiring slowed sharply in June and reinforced the US Federal Reserve could keep rates on hold.

IG market analyst Tony Sycamore said Australia’s “ripper” day was in response to the US jobs data.

“While this has boosted interest rate-sensitive sectors such as financials, real estate, and consumer-facing names, the largest response today has come from the heavyweight Materials sector,” he said.

“This is because commodity prices are negatively correlated with the US dollar, and with the greenback coming off the boil overnight after the softer US jobs data, there has been a solid bounce in commodity prices.”

On a strong day nine of the 11 sectors finished higher led by interest sensitive banks and mining stocks.

The day was dominated by the gold producers as the safe haven commodity climbed 1.3 per cent to $US4170 an ounce ($A6004) which led to Northern Star surged 11.75 per cent to $22.16, Evolution Mining rallied 8.83 per cent to $12.82 and Newmont jumped 4.98 per cent to $142.17.

It was also a strong day for the big four banks led by Commonwealth Bank which rallied 2.41 per cent to $165.02, while Westpac added 0.65 per cent to $35.69, National Australia Bank moved up 0.42 per cent to $38.57 and ANZ jumped 1.35 per cent to $35.26.

Mr Sycamore also pointed out three of the big four banks paid dividends in the last week adding to investor sentiment.

“This has delivered a welcome cash injection for investors, much of which often finds its way back into the market,” he said.

Vaccines giant CSL also jumped 3.45 per cent to $121.81, Sigma Healthcare rallied 2.20 per cent to $2.79 and Pro Medicus closed 1.81 per cent higher to $209.65.

In company news Australian property exchange platform operator Pexa share price slumped 21.29 per cent to $8.54 after flagging revenue hit from the NSW regulator proposed fee cuts. This would strip around $70m from its annual revenue.

Insurance giant Suncorp shares fell 3.72 per cent to $18.63 after telling the market investment income will be lower in financial year 2026 compared with earlier guidance, while it also flagged natural hazards will cost an additional $250m.

Securities exchange operator ASX shares fell 1.40 per cent to $51.52 after the federal court approved a $20.5m penalty over misleading statements on its technology upgrade project.

Boss Energy shares rallied 7.14 per cent to $1.28 thanks to the company meeting its revised 2025-2026 production guidance.

Northern Star resources soared 11.75 per cent to $22.16 and Pexa share price slumped 21.29 per cent to $8.54
